hints.content:
$f$ is decreasing in an interval where as $x$ increases, $f(x)$ decreases.

Visually, this is where the graph is going downwards as we go from left to right.



[[☃ image 1]]

options.alt: A coordinate plane. The x-axis scales by one, and the y-axis scales by eight. The continuous curve from left to right passes through the point negative five, forty and the point negative three point five, zero. Then, there's a local minimum at negative two point five, negative ten followed by an x-intercept at negative one, zero. The curve continues to the y-intercept zero, fourteen and a local maximum at one point seven-five, twenty-eight. The curve heads towards the point three point seven, zero, and four point five, negative forty. All of these values are estimated. The function is highlighted from x equals negative five to two point five and from x equals one point seven-five to five.

hints.content:
Now we can check each option:

Interval | Is $f$ decreasing on the interval?
:-: | :-:
$-5<x<-2.5$ | $\greenD{\text{Yes!}}$
$-2.5<x<1.75$ | $\redD{\text{No}}$. $f$ is increasing on this interval
$1.75<x<5$ | $\greenD{\text{Yes!}}$
